subject: Clarify order schedule true-up waterfall and SKU packaging mapping
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@acmecloud.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sabrina Lee <sabrina.lee@acmecloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:48:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on order schedule true-up and SKU mapping

Jordan —

Thanks for the updated order schedule and the pricing exhibit. We reviewed Exhibit B and have a couple of calls-out before we can approve the redline:

1) True-up waterfall: the way the "annual true-up" is defined (section 3.2) seems to start from "committed tokens" but then references "effective utilization" which doesn't match the metric in the invoice example. Can you confirm the anchor (committed vs billed peak) used to compute the waterfall tiers?

2) Packaging / SKU mapping: our billing system expects SKU-level granularity for the bundle (base + add-ons). The order schedule shows a single line item for the package with a cap/floor applied. We need a mapping table so our AR can reconcile usage to invoice lines.

3) Price protection window: the 90-day stabilization clause in the pricing guardrail appears to allow a mid-term reprice prior to the true-up period. Is that intentional? If so, we'd want to document how credits/refunds flow.

Attached is a redline PDF annotated with line comments (ACME_OrderSchedule_annotated.pdf). Can you and your legal team propose language that keeps the economic protections while giving us SKU mapping for billing?

Appreciate a short call if that helps — Sabrina and I are available Wed morning PT.

Thanks,
Liam
---
Liam O'Connor
Head of Cloud Economics, Acme Cloud
liam@acmecloud.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on order schedule true-up and SKU mapping

Liam —

Thanks for the thorough notes and the annotated PDF. Quick answers up front:
- Anchor for the waterfall should be "committed monthly equivalent" (CME) as defined in the glossary — sorry for the cross-reference gap in the draft. We'll make that explicit.
- We can provide a SKU mapping table as an appendix that expands the single line-item into the invoice-level SKUs (base SKU + add-ons + per-token surcharges). This won't change the economic caps/floors but will give Acme the reconciliation you need.
- The 90-day protection clause was included to allow temporary promotional pricing that can't be withdrawn within that window. We can clarify the credit/refund flow so that any mid-term reductions are reconciled at the next true-up rather than creating immediate prorated refunds.

I'm looping in Karthik (legal) and Marissa (your AE) to draft compromise language. If helpful, let's do a 30-minute walkthrough Wednesday 10:00 AM PT — I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Sales Lead — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acmecloud.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on order schedule true-up and SKU mapping

Liam —

Appreciate the clear asks. A few practical proposals from the commercial side that should address Acme's AR needs while preserving our pricing guardrails:

- SKU Appendix: we'll add Appendix C — "SKU Mapping & Invoice Lines" — with three rows: Base Package SKU (monthly commit), Add-on: Embeddings SKU (per-1k tokens), Add-on: Dedicated Throughput (burst). Each row will include the invoice code Acme can ingest. This appendix is informational and doesn't alter the caps/floors math.

- True-up Definition: propose replacing ambiguous text with: "True-up reconciliation shall be performed annually using Committed Monthly Equivalent (CME), defined as the average of committed units over the preceding 12 months, subject to the guardrail caps/floors in Exhibit B." That should align definitions.

- Mid-term Price Protection: change the line to read: "Promotional pricing reductions within a 90-day window will be applied prospectively to future invoices and reconciled at the next annual true-up; such reductions do not trigger retroactive refunds except as required by applicable law."

I'll have Karthik convert the above into redline language (short, trackable edits) and attach. If that sounds good to you I'll send the calendar invite for Wednesday 10:00 AM PT and circulate the redline.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on order schedule true-up and SKU mapping — redline attached

Liam —

Thanks for the call earlier. Per discussion, attached is a concise legal redline (AS-Exhibit-Price-Redline.docx) that implements the three commercial fixes we agreed on: explicit CME anchor, Appendix C SKU mapping (informational), and clarified promotional pricing flow (applied prospectively; reconciled at annual true-up).

Key snippets included in the redline:
• Section 3.2 (True-up): "For purposes of reconciliation, 'Committed Monthly Equivalent' (CME) shall mean the 12-month rolling average of committed units as specified in the Order Schedule. All true-up calculations shall reference CME and apply the caps/floors matrix in Exhibit B as of the reconciliation date."
• Appendix C (SKU Mapping): table with invoice codes and a note: "Appendix C is informational and for billing reconciliation only; economic caps/floors in Exhibit B remain controlling."
• Section 6.4 (Promotional Pricing): "Temporary price reductions offered to Customer shall remain in effect for a minimum of ninety (90) calendar days and, where such reduction results in net credits due to over-collection, such credits will be reflected in the next annual true-up reconciliation unless otherwise required by law."

I also uploaded the DocuSign-ready Order Form to the shared link: RDW-ACME_Docusign_OrderForm.url. Please review and let us know any last comments by EOD Friday so we can route for signatures next week.

Attachments: AS-Exhibit-Price-Redline.docx (legal redline), ACME_OrderSchedule_annotated.pdf (ACME comments).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
